identity.title: VideoRoPE: What Makes for Good Video Rotary Position Embedding?

problem.claim: Adapting 1D Rotary Position Embedding to videos with complex spatio-temporal structure.

gap.claim: Prior work had not fully considered four characteristics identified as essential for effective video RoPE adaptation; existing variants could be misled by periodic distractors when temporal dimension allocation was inappropriate.

contributions.claim: A comprehensive analysis identifying four characteristics considered essential for adapting RoPE to video.
V-NIAH-D, a Visual Needle-In-A-Haystack task augmented with periodic distractors.
VideoRoPE, a 3D RoPE design using low-frequency temporal allocation, diagonal spatial layout, and adjustable temporal spacing.

stated_novelty.claim: The work presents an analysis centered on four previously underconsidered characteristics, introduces V-NIAH-D, and derives the VideoRoPE design from that analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that V-NIAH-D shows previous RoPE variants are easily misled by periodic distractors when temporal dimension allocation is inappropriate.
The authors report that VideoRoPE consistently surpasses previous RoPE variants on long video retrieval, video understanding, and video hallucination tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames video adaptation of 1D RoPE as difficult because video has complex spatio-temporal structure.
It identifies four key characteristics and introduces V-NIAH-D with periodic distractors to expose temporal-allocation weaknesses.
It proposes VideoRoPE, combining 3D structure, low-frequency temporal allocation, diagonal spatial layout, and adjustable temporal spacing.
The authors report consistent superiority over prior RoPE variants across several video tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a targeted distractor-based task to a specific design weakness—temporal dimension allocation—and then describes method components addressing temporal oscillation, spatial symmetry, and index coupling.

lessons.interpretation: A focused stress test can make architectural design choices diagnostically interpretable.
lessons.application: When proposing a structured positional encoding, design an evaluation perturbation that isolates the suspected failure mode and map each component to a measured or described issue.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the perturbation does not represent the deployment setting or cannot distinguish among competing design explanations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four characteristics individually.
It provides no dataset names, quantitative margins, baselines beyond unspecified prior RoPE variants, or experimental conditions for the reported comparisons.
The abstract does not state whether the code and model weights were actually released.
